weechat-radio:$ Band plan

      
Where WeeChat Radio sits on each band. Every bar is one band, edge to edge, and the marks are the spots the app suggests: the same list as calling frequencies and wcr help calling.


      

        
Check your licence first

        
You are the control operator. The edges here are the widest allocation the app knows, and your country may allow less. Verify the frequency, mode and power for your licence before you transmit.

      


      

        
How the spots were picked

        
    
          
  • Inside the data or digital part of each band plan, so long data bursts stay out of the voice and CW segments.
  • Next to the busy automated spots (FT8, JS8, APRS) where the plan allows, not on them. 60m and 17m are too small to avoid FT8.
  • One spot per band and region, so stations find each other without agreeing a frequency first.
  • On licence-free bands and CB, channel 1 or the national calling channel: every set can tune it, and people already listen there.
  • Mode follows the radio: USB data on HF and SSB CB, FM on VHF, UHF and FM CB sets, AM where typical CB sets are AM only.
    •

              11115161919353638
            

            
26.96527.405

            
UK
  • 27.135 USB CEPT ch 15 hf-poor
  • 27.185 FM CEPT ch 19 vhf-fm
  • 27.781 FM UK ch 19 vhf-fm
Channel 19 is the calling channel on both the CEPT band and the older UK 27/81 band. SSB sets use channel 15, away from it.
EU
  • 27.135 USB ch 15 hf-poor
  • 27.185 FM ch 19 vhf-fm
Channel 19 is the common FM calling and road channel. SSB sets use channel 15, away from it.
DE
  • 26.565 FM ch 41 vhf-fm
  • 26.965 FM ch 1 vhf-fm
Germany has 80 channels. Channel 1 is a common FM calling channel for German speakers; channel 41 starts the extra channels below it.
US/CA
  • 27.185 AM ch 19 vox-safe
  • 27.365 USB ch 36 hf-poor
  • 27.385 LSB ch 38 hf-poor
Channel 19 is the road channel almost every AM set listens to. Sideband sets use 36 (USB) and 38 (LSB, the usual SSB calling channel).
AU
  • 27.085 AM ch 11 vox-safe
  • 27.155 LSB ch 16 hf-poor
  • 27.355 LSB ch 35 hf-poor
  • 27.355 USB ch 35 hf-poor
Channels 11 (AM) and 16 (SSB) are the official calling channels. Channel 35 is where SSB DX contacts gather.
NZ
  • 26.720 LSB 26ch 35 hf-poor
  • 27.085 AM ch 11 vox-safe
  • 27.355 USB ch 35 hf-poor
Channel 11 AM and channel 35 SSB match Australia. NZ also has a 26 MHz band below the common channels, with its own channel 35.

            
Licence-free. Calling channels differ by country, so each country has its own picks. The full bar covers every regional plan the app knows: NZ 26 MHz, the German extra channels below channel 1, and the UK 27/81 band above.

More

        
The preset under each spot is where to start. On a rough HF path use hf-weak or hf-deep instead of hf-poor. See weak signals.

        
Stations on different bands still chat through a gateway and the hub. See cross-frequency chat and one group across PMR, CB, 2m and internet.
